title: Full diagram coverage for guide chapters 7, 9, and 10
problem: The methodology site's canonical guide reaches B+ visual density only through chapter 5. Chapters 7 (Agents), 9 (Risk classification), and 10 (Failure handling) are pure prose and tables, which under-serves concepts that earlier chapters illuminate visually. The original spec (§8.7) targeted one signature diagram and one structural diagram per major chapter — roughly 13 diagrams total — but the three chapters named here ship zero, leaving a gap between the spec intent and the published guide.
solution: Add at least one production-ready diagram per target chapter that visually carries each chapter's central concept, matching chapter 3's level of polish. Chapter 7's agent-role grouping by phase (Discovery vs Delivery) calls for a phase-partitioned layout; chapter 9's deterministic binary classification calls for a decision-gate shape showing inputs funnelling to a Fast Lane or Full Pipeline output; chapter 10's three failure categories with distinct response shapes call for a parallel or stacked treatment. Each diagram is built from existing primitive components (StepRow, StepArrow, Popover, FlowArrow, FloatingLegend) where possible; new composite components (AgentMatrix, DecisionGate, or similar) are introduced only where existing layouts cannot accommodate the chapter's concept without distortion. All diagrams follow the established aesthetic constraints: #F4F1EC / #0D1421 / #2D5F4E palette, Fraunces + IBM Plex Sans + JetBrains Mono, native <details> popovers, single content-column horizontal extent, zero client-side JS. The three chapters map to three independent peer tasks in the Plan, exercising /cloverleaf-run-plan's max_concurrent: 3 default end-to-end. All three tasks touch site/ and are classified risk_class: high (full pipeline, including UI Reviewer and QA). New baselines are captured per browser (chromium, webkit, firefox) at all configured viewports; the existing affected-routes.json entry mapping site/src/content/guide/** to /guide/ covers the new content without amendment.
unknowns: For chapter 7 (Agents), does TrackDiagram.astro's fixed two-column left/right layout with a FlowArrow centre column cleanly express agents grouped by Discovery vs Delivery phase, or is a new AgentMatrix component (two labelled columns, no cross-track arrow) necessary to avoid visual distortion?

For chapter 9 (Risk classification), no existing component expresses binary branching with multiple inputs converging on a decision node. Does SingleTrack extended with a fork annotation satisfy the concept, or does a new DecisionGate component provide a materially clearer rendering without exceeding the diagram budget?

For chapter 10 (Failure handling), does the three-category structure (mechanical / quality / strategic) fit best as three sequential SingleTrack instances, a three-column TrackDiagram variant, or a new stacked layout? What component shape keeps the diagram self-contained without exceeding the ~13-diagram cap?

What minimum viewport width should trigger a collapse from each new diagram's grid/flex layout to a list or table fallback? The existing components contain no @media breakpoints in their scoped styles and global.css declares no breakpoints; the correct threshold must be established before implementation to ensure mobile-responsive behaviour at 375px.
acceptance_criteria: Chapters 7, 9, and 10 each ship at least one diagram that visually carries the chapter's central concept at chapter 3's level of polish.
Existing chapters 3, 4, and 5 and all other pages (/, /start, /faq) are visually unchanged, confirmed by visual-diff pass against existing chromium baselines.
npm run build in site/ succeeds with zero warnings.
Lighthouse score on /guide/ is not worse than the v1 baseline on Performance, Accessibility, Best Practices, and SEO.
New visual baselines are captured for /guide/ across chromium, webkit, and firefox at the three configured viewports (375/768/1280).
Total diagram count across the guide does not exceed 13 (the §8.7 cap).
All new diagrams use only native <details> for any interactive elements; no client-side JS is introduced.
The Plan emits a task_dag with three independent peer tasks (one per chapter) so /cloverleaf-run-plan exercises max_concurrent: 3 parallelism on this real-project Discovery output.
All three tasks carry risk_class: high, confirmed before Plan finalises.
out_of_scope: Refactoring or modifying existing components (SignatureLoop, TrackDiagram, SingleTrack) unless a Spike surfaces a blocking issue.
Dark theme, search, sitemap, OG image, and custom domain.
Spec edits — §8.7 already mandates B+ density; this RFC executes on it.
Amending affected-routes.json — the existing contentRoutes entry already maps site/src/content/guide/** to /guide/.
